```
$ python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_canonical_backfill_f002.py -q
$ python -m pytest scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_invocation_ledger.py scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_invocation_ledger_canonical.py scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_canonical_evidence_f006.py -q
```

**[high, correctness] Forgeable held-lock proof** — `HeldLedgerLock` was a public dataclass that could be constructed directly with `active=True` and would then `authorize` a write. I made it unforgeable: added a process-private `_LOCK_GUARD` sentinel that only `hold_ledger_lock()` (the C8 sole-owner seam) holds, and a `__post_init__` that raises `RuntimeError` unless that exact sentinel is passed. The auditor's exact attack — `HeldLedgerLock('/tmp/x', active=True)` — now raises at construction instead of yielding an authorizing token; the genuine `hold_ledger_lock()` seam still mints a working token. New test `test_held_lock_proof_is_unforgeable` (plus a positive control) locks this in.

**[medium, correctness] Lock refusal happened after evidence loading** — In `run_backfill`, write-mode validated/loa
